::: {.project-hook}
Analysed how AI adoption reshapes labour demand across the skill distribution in the United States—and proposed a policy to help workers adapt—for the Berkeley High School Essay Contest.
:::

## Contest prompt

::: {.prompt-block}
*The Economics of Artificial Intelligence:* Artificial intelligence is expected to affect workers differently across the skill distribution. Analyze how AI adoption may reshape labor demand for high-skill, middle-skill, and low-skill workers in the United States, considering both productivity-enhancing and displacement effects. Discuss how these impacts might influence wage inequality. Propose and critically evaluate one specific policy designed to help workers adapt to AI-driven changes.
:::

## Overview

This essay examines the dual forces of AI on the labour market—productivity enhancement for high-skill workers and displacement risk for middle- and low-skill roles—and traces the implications for wage inequality. It then proposes and critically evaluates a specific adaptation policy, weighing feasibility against equity outcomes.

## What I did

::: {.project-section}
<ul class="star-list">
<li><strong>Situation:</strong> AI is reshaping labour markets globally, but policy responses remain contested—especially for workers at different points on the skill ladder.</li>
<li><strong>Task:</strong> Write a rigorous economics essay analysing AI's differential impact on high-, middle-, and low-skill workers, and propose a credible adaptation policy.</li>
<li><strong>Action:</strong> Researched labour economics literature on skill-biased technological change; structured arguments around productivity versus displacement effects; designed and critically evaluated a targeted worker-adaptation policy.</li>
<li><strong>Result:</strong> Submitted the completed essay to the [Berkeley High School Essay Contest](https://econreview.studentorg.berkeley.edu/high-school-essay/){target="_blank"} on 8 March 2026, responding to Prompt 1 on the economics of AI.</li>
</ul>
:::
